title: Which Workers Feel the Most Stress
paragraphs: Stress at work is common around the world. But some workers feel much more stress than others, according to Gallup's 2026 State of the Global Workplace report.
The report is based on surveys of workers in 160 countries. It asks people about their feelings at work, including whether they felt a lot of stress during the previous day.

In Europe, workers in southern countries reported the most stress. In Greece, 61% of workers said they felt stressed. Greece was followed by Malta at 57%, Cyprus at 56%, Italy at 51% and Spain at 47%. Workers in Denmark felt the least stress, at just 19%, followed by Poland at 22% and Lithuania at 23%.
The report also looked at which types of workers are most stressed. In Europe, the most stressed workers tend to be managers who are under 35 and who work partly at home and partly in the office.

In Southeast Asia, workers in the Philippines were the most stressed. Half of Filipino workers said they had felt stress for much of the previous day. That is double the Southeast Asian average of 25%, and above the global average of 40%.

Europe as a whole was less stressed than the Americas. In fact, the report found that the US and Canada have both the most engaged and the most stressed workers in the world. Being engaged means feeling excited about and involved in your work.

Overall, engagement around the world is falling. Only 20% of workers globally said they felt engaged at work, the lowest level since 2020. It was also the first time global engagement had fallen for two years in a row.
According to Gallup, stressed or unengaged workers have a big effect on the world economy. It estimates that the lost productivity could be worth up to 9% of the world's total economic output.
